-듯하다 用在 \"피곤한 듯해요\" 这样的句子中，用于谨慎推测对方状态。\\.en: -듯하다 is used in sentences like "피곤한 듯해요" to cautiously guess about someone's condition.\n-모양이다 is used in sentences like "비가 올 모양이에요", often to predict based on observing the weather or situation.

推测前提下的期待/担忧，以及\"叫某人/对某人\"的表达.en: Expressing expectation or concern based on a supposition, and "telling someone / to someone"

-을/ㄹ 텐데 在推测或预料某种状况的前提下，表达说话者的期待、担忧或遗憾，相当.en: -을/ㄹ 텐데 expresses the speaker's expectation, concern, or regret based on a supposition or anticipated situation, equivalent to "should be... / must be... (so...)".\n-더러/보고 both indicate the recipient of an action, equivalent to "tell... / say to...", mainly used in commands, requests, or relaying messages. 더러 is slightly more formal than 보고.

-을/ㄹ 텐데：动词/形容词 词干 + (으)ㄹ 텐데（有收音 + 을 텐데，无.en: -을/ㄹ 텐데: verb/adjective stem + (으)ㄹ 텐데 (with final consonant + 을 텐데, without final consonant or with ㄹ + ㄹ 텐데)\n더러/보고: noun (person) + 더러/보고 + verb (command/request sentence)

-을/ㄹ 텐데 前句主语可以是说话人自己或第三人称。后面接请求、担忧、建议等。\.en: The subject of the preceding clause with -을/ㄹ 텐데 can be the speaker or a third person. It is followed by requests, concerns, suggestions, etc.\n더러/보고 must be preceded by a person noun; things or abstract nouns cannot be used.

-을/ㄹ 텐데 常用于体谅对方，如 \"피곤할 텐데 쉬세요\"。\\n더러/보.en: -을/ㄹ 텐데 is often used to show consideration for the other person, e.g., "피곤할 텐데 쉬세요".\n더러/보고 is often used with verbs of relaying (말하다/시키다/부탁하다), e.g., "누구보고 가라고 했어？".

确认共识，或补充说明理由.en: Confirming shared knowledge, or adding explanatory reasons

-잖아요 用于确认说话双方都知道的事实，带有\"你不是知道吗/你看……不是……嘛.en: -잖아요 is used to confirm facts both the speaker and listener know, carrying a tone of "you know, right? / see, isn't it...?", implying the listener should already be aware of the information.\n-거든요 is used to add background information or reasons the speaker thinks the listener doesn't know, equivalent to "because... (you might not know) / actually...", with a softer tone than -니까, giving a slight explanatory feel.

-잖아요：动词/形容词/이다 词干 + 잖아요（现在），+ 았/었잖아요（过去）.en: -잖아요: verb/adjective/이다 stem + 잖아요 (present), + 았/었잖아요 (past)\n-거든요: verb/adjective/이다 stem + 거든요 (present), + 았/었거든요 (past)

-잖아요 用于说话人和听话人共享的信息。用于听话人完全不知道的信息时不自然。\\.en: -잖아요 is used for information shared between the speaker and the listener. It sounds unnatural when used with information the listener doesn't know at all.\n-거든요 is used to tell the listener information that only the speaker knows. It can be used alone at the end of a sentence or in a reason clause.

-잖아요 用在 \"그 사람 알잖아요！（你认识那个人的嘛！）\" 这样的句子中.en: -잖아요 is used in sentences like "그 사람 알잖아요! (You know that person, right!)" and is also used for mild protest or to draw attention.\n-거든요 is used in sentences like "사실 저 한국 사람이거든요 (Actually, I'm Korean)" and is often used to naturally introduce new background information.

表示把某动作的结果转移或提供给他人.en: Indicates transferring or providing the result of an action to someone else

-아/어/여다 주다 表示做完某动作后把结果给对方，相当于\"……给……/帮…….en: -아/어/여다 주다 means doing an action and then giving the result to someone, equivalent to "...for someone / do something for someone." Compared to -아/어/여 주다, it adds a sense of movement, like "bringing/taking the result."\n-아/어/여다 드리다 is the honorific form, used for elders or people of higher status.\nIt is often used with verbs of movement like "사다 주다 (buy and give)" "가져다주다 (bring and give)" "데려다주다 (take someone to)".

-아/어/여다 주다：动词词干 + 아/어/여다 주다\\n词干元音为 ㅏ/ㅗ.en: -아/어/여다 주다: verb stem + 아/어/여다 주다\nIf the stem vowel is ㅏ/ㅗ → 아다, otherwise → 어다, 하다 verbs → 여다 (해다)\n-아/어/여다 드리다: replace 주다 with 드리다 (honorific)

-아/어/여다 주다 vs -아/어 주다：前者带有把结果送过去的移动语气，后者.en: -아/어/여다 주다 vs -아/어 주다: the former carries a sense of moving the result over, while the latter simply means helping or doing a favor.\nWhen speaking to elders, replace 주다 with the honorific 드리다: 가져다 드리다, 사다 드리다.

-아/어/여다 주다 常与\"사다 주다（买来给）\"\"가져다주다（拿来给）\.en: -아/어/여다 주다 is often used with verbs of movement like "사다 주다 (buy and give)" "가져다주다 (bring and give)" "데려다주다 (take someone to)".

表示做完某动作后来/回来，或连续动作.en: Indicates coming/returning after doing something, or a sequence of actions

-아/어다 오다 表示做完某事后来（到说话现场），相当于\"做了……来了/带来了.en: -아/어다 오다 means doing something and then coming (to the speaker's location), equivalent to "did... and came/brought it," emphasizing that the result is here.\n-아/어다 주다 in this lesson focuses on reviewing the direction of movement in "bring and give": 오다 emphasizes movement toward the speaker, while 가다 emphasizes movement away from the speaker.\nThe core variable in both expressions is the direction of movement: 사다 오다 (buy and come/bring), 사다 가다 (buy and go/take).

动词 词干 + 아/어다 오다/가다\\n词干 元音 ㅏ/ㅗ → 아다，그 외.en: Verb stem + 아/어다 오다/가다\nStem vowel ㅏ/ㅗ → 아다, otherwise → 어다\nDirection: 오다 (toward speaker) vs 가다 (away from speaker)

-아/어다 오다 与 -아/어다 가다 的区别在于移动方向。以说话人位置为基准，.en: The difference between -아/어다 오다 and -아/어다 가다 lies in the direction of movement. Based on the speaker's position, determine whether the result comes toward or goes away.\nWhen combined with 주다/드리다, it belongs to the 오다 series: bringing the result to the speaker's side.

像\"밥을 해다 오다（做了饭来）\"\"빨래를 해다 가다（洗了衣服去）\"这.en: Like "밥을 해다 오다 (cook and come)" or "빨래를 해다 가다 (do laundry and go)," this often appears in household chore actions.

表示惊讶/反问，或强调\"当然是/那还用说\".en: Expresses surprise/rhetorical question, or emphasizes "of course/needless to say"

-다니요 用于对听到的内容表示惊讶、意外或质疑，相当于\"竟然……？/……这是什.en: -다니요 is used to express surprise, disbelief, or questioning about something heard, equivalent to "...really?/What do you mean by...?" It is a reactive follow-up question to the previous statement.\n-고 말고요 is used to strongly affirm the other person's suggestion or question, equivalent to "Of course.../Needless to say..." with a firm and positive tone.

-다니요：动词/形容词基本形（终止形）+ 다니요，이다 → 이라니요，있다/없다.en: -다니요: Verb/adjective basic form (ending form) + 다니요, 이다 → 이라니요, 있다/없다 → 있다니요/없다니요\n-고 말고요: Verb/adjective stem + 고 말고요 (unconditional affirmation)

-다니요 原样重复或引用对方的话语来表示惊讶，接近直接引用。\\n-고 말고요.en: -다니요 repeats or quotes the other person's words as-is to express surprise, similar to direct quotation.\n-고 말고요 is a strong affirmation to a question, more emotional than "물론이죠". It can be used alone or attached to a sentence.

-다니요 如\"그게 사실이라니요！（那竟是真的？！）\"，常用于震惊或难以置信.en: -다니요: e.g., "그게 사실이라니요! (That's actually true?!)", often used in shocking or unbelievable situations.\n-고 말고요: e.g., "같이 가고 말고요! (Of course, let's go together!)", used to enthusiastically agree with someone's suggestion.

表示状态/动作从过去持续到现在，或向未来延续.en: Indicates a state/action continuing from the past to the present, or extending into the future

-아/어 오다 表示某状态或动作从过去持续到现在，相当于\"一直……到现在/…….en: -아/어 오다 indicates that a state or action has continued from the past to the present, equivalent to "has been... until now/...has come about", emphasizing that the arrival point of change is the present.\n-아/어 가다 indicates that a state or action continues from the present into the future, equivalent to "becoming more and more.../gradually...", emphasizing that the direction of change is the future.\nThe core of both expressions is temporal direction: 오다 (past → present), 가다 (present → future).

动词/形容词词干 + 아/어 오다（过去→现在）\\n动词/形容词词干 + 아/.en: Verb/adjective stem + 아/어 오다 (past → present)\nVerb/adjective stem + 아/어 가다 (present → future)\nStem vowel ㅏ/ㅗ → 아, others → 어, 하다 → 해

-아/어 오다 主要与\"지금까지\"搭配，表示过去的持续。\\n-아/어 가다.en: -아/어 오다 is mainly used with "지금까지" to indicate continuation from the past.\n-아/어 가다 is used with "점점", "서서히", etc., to indicate change toward the future.

像\"한국어를 배워 오다（一直在学韩语）\" vs \"한국어 실력이 늘어.en: Like "한국어를 배워 오다 (have been learning Korean)" vs "한국어 실력이 늘어 가다 (Korean skills are improving)", even with the same topic, the temporal direction differs.

表示假装做某动作或处于某状态.en: Indicates pretending to do an action or be in a certain state

-는/은/ㄴ 체하다 和 -는/은/ㄴ 척하다 意思完全相同，均表示\"假装…….en: -는/은/ㄴ 체하다 and -는/은/ㄴ 척하다 have exactly the same meaning, both expressing "pretend to.../act as if...", indicating that it's not actually true, just putting on that appearance on the surface.\n척하다 is more common in spoken language, while 체하다 is slightly more formal/written. The two expressions can be used interchangeably.

动词现在冠词形（-는）+ 체하다/척하다\\n形容词/动词过去冠词形（-은/ㄴ）.en: Verb present adnominal form (-는) + 체하다/척하다\nAdjective/Verb past adnominal form (-은/ㄴ) + 체하다/척하다\nVerb/Adjective future adnominal form (-을/ㄹ) + 체하다/척하다

冠词形词尾选择：动词现在用 -는，动词/形容词过去用 -은/ㄴ，形容词现在用 -.en: Adnominal ending selection: verbs in present tense use -는, verbs/adjectives in past tense use -은/ㄴ, adjectives in present tense use -은/ㄴ\nBe careful not to confuse 체하다/척하다 with 체하다 meaning "indigestion" (체하다 = food stagnation, 척하다 = pretend).

像\"자는 척하다（假装睡觉）\"\"모르는 체하다（假装不知道）\"，是日常中.en: Expressions like "자는 척하다 (pretend to sleep)" or "모르는 체하다 (pretend not to know)" are commonly used in everyday conversation.

에 대해(서)，에 관해서，에 관한.en: 에 대해(서), 에 관해서, 에 관한

에 대해(서) 和 에 관해(서) 均表示\"关于……\"，用于指示谈论、研究、.en: 에 대해(서) and 에 관해(서) both mean "about...", used to indicate the object of discussion, research, or thought. Their meanings are very similar and they can be used interchangeably.\n에 관한/에 대한 are adnominal (attributive) forms used to modify the noun that follows, equivalent to "(noun) about...".\n에 대해서 is more colloquial, while 에 관해서 is more formal/written.

名词 + 에 대해（서）：动词前，\"关于……\"\\n名词 + 에 관해（서）.en:
Noun + 에 대해(서): before a verb, "about..."
Noun + 에 관해(서): before a verb, "about..." (more formal)
Noun + 에 관한/에 대한 + Noun: attributive form, "(noun) about..."

에 대해 和 에 관해 含义几乎相同，但 에 관해 在学术/报告等正式文体中更自.en:
에 대해 and 에 관해 have nearly the same meaning, but 에 관해 sounds more natural in formal contexts like academic writing or reports.
에 관한/에 대한 are attributive forms and must be followed by a noun. Use 에 대해/에 관해 before a verb.

\"환경에 대해 이야기하다\"，\"역사에 관한 책\"般，广泛用于发表、论文.en: Used widely in presentations, papers, news, and conversations, such as "환경에 대해 이야기하다" (talk about the environment) or "역사에 관한 책" (a book about history).

에 대해/에 관해 用法整理.en: Summary of 에 대해/에 관해 Usage

举例列举，或以某事为基准说\"光是……就……\".en: To list examples, or to use something as a baseline to say "just... already..."

을/를 비롯한 和 을/를 비롯해서 均表示\"以……为首/包括……在内\"，用.en:
을/를 비롯한 and 을/를 비롯해서 both mean "with... at the forefront/including..." and are used to list examples, indicating that something is a representative example among them.
비롯한 is the attributive form (modifier) and modifies the following noun; 비롯해서 is the connective form and is followed by a verb.
(까지)만 해도 means "just... already.../even just mentioning..." and uses a specific example to emphasize the overall degree, often carrying the nuance of "let alone the rest."

名词 + 을/를 비롯한 + 名词（以……为首的……）\\n名词 + 을/를 비.en:
Noun + 을/를 비롯한 + Noun (with... at the forefront)
Noun + 을/를 비롯해서 + Verb (including..., ...)
Noun + 만 해도 / Noun + 까지만 해도 (just... already...)

비롯한/비롯해서 前面的名词，是列举整体中的典型例子。\\n만 해도 举出一个极.en:
The noun before 비롯한/비롯해서 is a typical example within the overall list.
만 해도 gives an extreme example to emphasize the overall degree. 까지 is a stronger particle that further emphasizes the "extremeness."

\"BTS를 비롯한 K-POP 그룹들\"般，常用于先提出代表性例子的说明/发.en:
Used in explanations/presentations that first present a representative example, like "BTS를 비롯한 K-POP 그룹들" (K-pop groups including BTS).
Used in everyday conversation for exaggeration/emphasis, like "이것만 해도 너무 많아요" (Just this alone is already too much).

表示数量之多令人意外，或\"连……都/甚至……\".en: Indicates that a quantity is surprisingly large, or means "even.../including..."

개나（도）用在数量词后，表示说话人觉得该数量多得出乎意料，相当于\"竟然……个/.en: 개나(도) is used after a number or quantity word to express that the speaker finds the amount surprisingly large, equivalent to "as many as.../a whole...", with a slight tone of surprise or exaggeration.\n까지 is an emphatic particle meaning "even.../including...", emphasizing that something has reached an unexpected extreme, which can be either a pleasant surprise or an unpleasant shock.

수량 + 개나（도）：数量 + 개/명/권 + 나（도）（竟然……个）\\n名词.en: Quantity + 개나(도): number + 개/명/권 + 나(도) (as many as...)\nNoun/adverb + 까지: noun/adverb + 까지 (even.../including...)

개나 中的 나 表示\"比预期多\"的辅助语气。나/이나 后面不能再加 도（개나.en: In 개나, 나 adds the nuance of "more than expected." 나/이나 cannot be followed by 도 (개나도✗).\n까지 means "reaching an extreme." It is used for unexpected situations or extreme examples. The form of 까지 remains the same regardless of whether the preceding noun ends in a consonant or vowel.

\"이게 벌써 세 개나 됐어？（竟然已经三个了？）\"，\"친구까지 나를 의.en: Used to express surprise, as in "이게 벌써 세 개나 됐어? (It's already three of these?)" or "친구까지 나를 의심해 (Even my friend doubts me)."

나/이나 收音选择 / 까지 用法整理.en: 나/이나 Consonant/Vowel Selection / Summary of 까지 Usage

举例列举，或表示\"连最后的……都\".en: Used to list examples, or to mean "even the last..."

(이)라든가 和 (이)라든지 均用于列举若干例子，表示\"……啊/……之类的\.en: (이)라든가 and (이)라든지 are both used to list several examples, meaning "...or something like.../...and the like," indicating that it is not limited to one specific thing but is one of several examples. The two have the same meaning, with 라든지 being slightly more formal than 라든가.\n마저 means "even the last one/even what remains," emphasizing that even the final thing that should not have happened has occurred, carrying a sense of despair or regret, equivalent to "even... (the last hope/remaining one)."

收音O 名词 + 이라든가/이라든지\\n收音X 名词 + 라든가/라든지\\n.en: Noun ending in consonant + 이라든가/이라든지\nNoun ending in vowel + 라든가/라든지\nNoun + 마저 (even the last one...)

(이)라든가/(이)라든지 后面通常接动词或继续列举其他项。列举两个以上项目时，.en: (이)라든가/(이)라든지 is usually followed by a verb or continues listing other items. When listing two or more items, it is attached after each item.\n마저 expresses the despair that, in an already bad situation, even the last remaining thing has turned out this way. Its negative nuance is stronger than that of 까지.

\"영화라든가 음악이라든가（电影啊音乐之类的）\"般，列举兴趣时，\\n\"희.en: Like "영화라든가 음악이라든가" (movies, music, and the like) when listing interests, or "희망마저 없어졌어요" (even hope disappeared) to express a hopeless situation.

表示一面……一面……，或\"也会/也有\".en: Indicates "on one hand... on the other hand..." or "also/sometimes"

-는/은/ㄴ가 하면 表示两种对比或并列的情况同时存在，相当于\"一方面……另一.en: -는/은/ㄴ가 하면 expresses two contrasting or parallel situations coexisting, equivalent to "on one hand... on the other hand.../sometimes... sometimes...", often used to describe two sides of something.\n-기도 하다 indicates that in addition to a certain action or state, there are other situations, equivalent to "also/sometimes/also is", with a calm tone, often used with adverbs like 때로는 (sometimes).

-는/은/ㄴ가 하면：动词/形容词 冠词形 + 가 하면\\n-기도 하다：动词.en: -는/은/ㄴ가 하면: Verb/Adjective adnominal form + 가 하면\n-기도 하다: Verb/Adjective stem + 기도 하다

-는가 하면 前后分句是相互对照的内容。前句是一种情境，后句是相反或另一种情境。.en: In -는가 하면, the clauses before and after are contrasting. The first clause describes one situation, and the second describes an opposite or different one.\n-기도 하다 can be used alone (e.g., "~하기도 해요") or in a listing structure (e.g., "-기도 하고 -기도 하다").

如\"가격이 싼가 하면 품질이 나빠요（一方面价格便宜，另一方面质量不好）\".en: Like "가격이 싼가 하면 품질이 나빠요" (on one hand the price is cheap, on the other hand the quality is bad), or "슬프기도 하고 기쁘기도 해요" (I feel both sad and happy), used to describe complex emotions or situations.

-는/은/ㄴ가 하면 冠词形选择.en: Choosing the Adnominal Form for -는/은/ㄴ가 하면

P20 第1～5课 综合练习.en: Comprehensive practice for Lessons 1-5 of P20

如果当时……的话.en: If only it had been... (counterfactual about the past)

表达对过去已经发生（或未发生）的事情的反向假设。\\n和 -(으)면 不同：-(.en: Expresses a counterfactual assumption about something that already happened (or didn't happen) in the past.\nUnlike -(으)면, which describes general conditions, -았/었더라면 refers to an unchangeable past.\nThe second clause often pairs with -았을 텐데 / -았을 것이다 to express regret or speculation.

结构：过去词干（-았/었-）+ 더라면 + 后句（常用 -았을 텐데）。\\n前.en: Structure: past stem (-았/었-) + 더라면 + following clause (often with -았을 텐데).\nBoth clauses are in the past tense because the discussion is about a past that cannot be revisited.

判断口诀：一件事已经发生（或没发生），无法改变，只能\"想想当时如果……\"。\.en: Rule of thumb: If something has already happened (or hasn't) and cannot be changed, you can only "imagine what if..."\nThe key difference from -(으)면 is "whether it can be changed."\nIt's similar in meaning to -았/었으면 좋았을 텐데 but has a more formal tone.

早知道就……了（后悔没做）.en: I should have... (regret for not doing something)

表达说话人对\"当时没做某事\"的后悔。\\n和 -았/었더라면 不同：这里只对.en: Expresses the speaker's regret about "not having done something" at the time.\nUnlike -았/었더라면, this only expresses regret about the speaker's own actions, not about the situation itself.\nIn speech, 그랬다 is often omitted, leaving just -을걸 (with a drawn-out sound), conveying a self-muttering sense of remorse.

结构：动词词干（无收音 + ㄹ 걸；有收音 + 을 걸）+ 그랬다。\\n主语通.en: Structure: verb stem (no final consonant + ㄹ 걸; with final consonant + 을 걸) + 그랬다.\nThe subject is usually the speaker (first person), lamenting "I wish I had done it back then."

两个变体：\\n1. 完整形 -을/ㄹ 걸 그랬다：对听话人陈述后悔。\\n2..en: Two variants:\n1. Full form -을/ㄹ 걸 그랬다: states regret to the listener.\n2. Shortened form -을/ㄹ걸 (drawn-out): a self-muttering sigh of regret, with falling intonation at the end.

早知道就不该……（后悔做了）.en: I shouldn't have... (regret over doing something)

和上一课的 -을 걸 그랬다 相反，这个表示\"我当时不该做的\"的后悔。\\n.en: Opposite of -을 걸 그랬다 from the previous lesson, this expresses regret over "something I shouldn't have done."\nStructure: verb stem + 지 말 걸 그랬다, where 말다 = to not do (prohibit/stop).\nIn speech, it's often shortened to -지 말걸, carrying a self-reproachful tone.

结构：动词词干 + 지 말 걸 그랬다。\\n말다 是\"停止/不做\"的动词，.en: Structure: verb stem + 지 말 걸 그랬다.\n말다 is the verb for "to stop/not do," and adding -을 걸 gives 말 걸.\nThink of it as the negative version of -을 걸 그랬다.

\"应该做没做\" → -을 걸 그랬다\\n\"做了不该做\" → -지 말.en: "Should have done but didn't" → -을 걸 그랬다\n"Did something I shouldn't have" → -지 말 걸 그랬다\nThese two grammar points are paired—memorize them together for best results.

成对记忆：-을 걸 그랬다 vs -지 말 걸 그랬다.en: Paired Memory: -을 걸 그랬다 vs -지 말 걸 그랬다

-을 걸 그랬다 还是 -지 말 걸 그랬다？.en: -을 걸 그랬다 or -지 말 걸 그랬다?

本来应该……的（懊悔+义务感）.en: I should have... (regret + sense of obligation)

表达\"本来应当做某事，但实际上没做\"的懊悔。\\n和 -을 걸 그랬다 类似.en: Expresses regret over "something I should have done but didn't."\nSimilar to -을 걸 그랬다 but stronger in tone: it's not just regret, but also carries a sense of "it was my duty/responsibility."\nThe second half is often omitted, or followed by -지 못했어요 / 못 했어요 to state the actual outcome.

结构：动词过去词干（-았/었-）+ 어야 했는데。\\n可看作 -아/어야 하다.en: Structure: past verb stem (-았/었-) + 어야 했는데.\nCan be seen as the past + recollective form of -아/어야 하다 (must).\nThe subject can be yourself or someone else, making it more flexible than -을 걸 그랬다.

判断口诀：既有\"没做\"的懊悔，又有\"本该是义务\"的意味。\\n-을 걸.en: Memory tip: It combines regret over something not done with a sense of obligation.\n-을 걸 그랬다 leans toward personal wish, while -았어야 했는데 leans toward duty or responsibility.\nIt's also used when judging others: 너 그때 갔어야 했는데 (You should have gone then).

对过去情况的遗憾感叹，比 -았더라면 更口语化。\\n\"要是……就好了\" —.en: A regretful sigh about a past situation, more colloquial than -았더라면.\n"If only..." — in reality it didn't happen that way, so you can only sigh.\nSimilar in structure to -았더라면, but more commonly used in everyday conversation; -았더라면 leans toward written language.

结构：动词/形容词过去词干 + 으면 좋았을 텐데。\\n可看作 -았/었으면.en: Structure: verb/adjective past stem + 으면 좋았을 텐데.\nCan be seen as the past reflective form of -았/었으면 좋겠다 (hope).\nIt often stands alone as a sentence, or the latter half is omitted.

和 -았더라면 的选择：\\n1. 日常口语：-았으면 좋았을 텐데\\n2..en:
Choosing between -았더라면:
1. Everyday speech: -았으면 좋았을 텐데
2. Written/formal: -았더라면 -았을 텐데
The meaning is almost the same, and they can be used interchangeably.

表达\"差一点就发生了但幸好没发生\"。\\n主要功能是庆幸没发生某件（通常不好.en: Expresses "it almost happened, but fortunately it didn't."\nIts main function is to express relief that something (usually bad) didn't happen.\nThe structure is simple, but note: the verb before -을/ㄹ 뻔했다 always takes the future adnominal form.

结构：动词词干（无收音 + ㄹ；有收音 + 을）+ 뻔했다。\\n뻔하다 是\".en: Structure: verb stem (no final consonant + ㄹ; with final consonant + 을) + 뻔했다.\n뻔하다 is the fixed verb for "almost," always used in the past form 뻔했다.\nEven though it didn't happen, the future adnominal form is used because it "was about to" happen at that time.

这个语法看似简单，但学习者容易混淆两点：\\n1. 结尾必须是过去形 뻔했다，不.en: This grammar looks simple, but learners often confuse two points:\n1. The ending must be the past form 뻔했다, not 뻔한다 or 뻔해요.\n2. The preceding part uses the future adnominal form (-을/ㄹ), not the past adnominal form (-은/ㄴ).

对别人过去没做的事表达\"当时怎么不这样呢\"的责备+建议。\\n可以看作 -을.en: Expresses "why didn't you do it then" with reproach and advice about something the other person didn't do in the past.\nIt can be seen as the "for others" version of -을 걸 그랬다: one is self-reproach, the other addresses someone else.\nThe ending must be the past form 그랬어요, as it refers to "the other person's past choice of action."

结构：动词词干 + 지 그랬어요。\\n注意：-지 마세요（禁止）和 -지 그랬.en: Structure: verb stem + 지 그랬어요.\nNote: -지 마세요 (prohibition) and -지 그랬어요 (reproach) look similar, but their meanings are completely different.\nIt only attaches to verbs, not adjectives.

和 -을 걸 그랬다 配对：\\n1. 自责：-을 걸 그랬다（我该……的）\\.en:
Pairs with -을 걸 그랬다:
1. Self-reproach: -을 걸 그랬다 (I should have...)
2. Reproaching others: -지 그랬어요 (Why didn't you...)

Completely different from -지 마세요: -지 마세요 = please don't do; -지 그랬어요 = why didn't you do it then.

自责 vs 责别人：语法配对表.en: Self-Reproach vs. Reproaching Others: Grammar Pairing Table

表达\"即使过去做了/是了，结果也不会变\"的让步语气。\\n和 -아/어도（即.en: Expresses a concessive tone meaning "even if (something) had been done or had happened in the past, the result wouldn't have changed."\nIt is the past counterfactual version of -아/어도 (even if).\nOften used with -았을 것이다 / -았을 텐데 to emphasize that "changing the past wouldn't have helped."

结构：动词/形容词过去词干（-았/었-）+ 어도。\\n跟第一课 -았더라면 结.en:
Structure: verb/adjective past stem (-았/었-) + 어도.
Similar in structure to -았더라면 from Lesson 1, but opposite in meaning:
· -았더라면 = "if (something) had happened" (hypothetical change)
· -았어도 = "even if (something) had happened" (change wouldn't have helped)

判断口诀：\\n· 假设改变过去，好结果会发生 → -았더라면\\n· 假设改变.en:
Quick rule of thumb:
· Hypothesizing a change in the past that would lead to a good result → -았더라면
· Hypothesizing a change in the past that still wouldn't improve the outcome → -았어도
The second clause usually carries a negative or unfavorable meaning.

完成这份练习，检验假设与后悔八大语法是否掌握。\\n共 10 题，覆盖 -았더라.en: Complete this practice to test your mastery of the eight grammar points for hypotheses and regrets.\nThere are 10 questions covering -았더라면, -을 걸 그랬다, -지 말 걸 그랬다, -았어야 했는데, -았으면 좋았을 텐데, -을 뻔했다, -지 그랬어요, and -았어도.

P21 假设与后悔八大语法：\\n1. -았더라면（书面反事实）\\n2. -을.en:
P21's eight grammar points for hypotheses and regrets:
1. -았더라면 (written counterfactual)
2. -을 걸 그랬다 (self-blame for not doing something you should have)
3. -지 말 걸 그랬다 (self-blame for doing something you shouldn't have)
4. -았어야 했는데 (obligation/responsibility-type regret)
5. -았으면 좋았을 텐데 (colloquial past lament)
6. -을 뻔했다 (almost / nearly)
7. -지 그랬어요 (blaming others for not doing something in the past)
8. -았어도 (past counterfactual concession)

综合练习 · 假设与后悔八大语法.en: Comprehensive Practice · Eight Grammar Points for Hypotheses and Regrets

表达对某种（不希望发生的）情况的担心。\\n后半句通常是为避免这个担心而采取的行.en: Expresses worry about an (unwanted) situation.\nThe second half of the sentence is usually an action taken to avoid that worry.\nExtremely common in both speech and writing—it's the most important "worry expression" in Korean.

结构：动词/形容词词干（无收音+ㄹ；有收音+을）+ 까 봐。\\n可看作 -을까.en: Structure: verb/adjective stem (no batchim + ㄹ; with batchim + 을) + 까 봐.\nCan be seen as a blend of -을까? (whether it will) + 봐 (worry), literally "seeing whether..."\nThe second half often contains actions like 걱정하다, 안 하다, 챙기다, 준비하다 to avoid the worry.

常见搭配套路：\\n1. -을까 봐 걱정이에요（担心……）\\n2. -을까.en:
Common patterns:
1. -을까 봐 걱정이에요 (worried that...)
2. -을까 봐 [action] (afraid that... so I did...)
3. -을까 봐서 (connective form, adding 서 to emphasize the reason)
Past tense uses -았/었을까 봐 (was afraid that... at the time).

表达低概率的推测，\"说不定会……\"、\"没准儿……\"。\\n比 -을 것.en: Expresses a low-probability guess: "might...", "could be..."\nWeaker and more uncertain than -을 것 같다 (seems like), just suggesting a possibility.\nCarries the nuance of "I'm not sure, but maybe"—a high-frequency expression in intermediate Korean.

结构：动词/形容词词干（无收音+ㄹ；有收音+을）+ 지도 모르다。\\n直译\".en: Structure: verb/adjective stem (no batchim + ㄹ; with batchim + 을) + 지도 모르다.\nLiterally "don't even know (whether)...", extended to mean "might"\nCommon endings: 몰라요 / 모르겠어요, which sound more polite and tentative.

推测的确定性梯度（从低到高）：\\n1. -을지도 모르다（说不定）— 最不确定.en:
Certainty scale (from low to high):
1. -을지도 모르다 (might) — least certain
2. -을 수도 있다 (could also) — objective possibility
3. -을 것 같다 (seems like) — some feeling
4. -을 것이다 (probably will) — fairly sure
5. -을 게 틀림없다 (must be) — most certain

不可能……（强烈否定推测）.en: It can't be... (strongly negating a possibility)

强烈否定某种可能性：\"那怎么可能\"、\"不可能\"。\\n和 -을 리가 있.en: Strongly denies a possibility: "How could that be?" or "No way."\nIt pairs with -을 리가 있어요? (rhetorical question), both expressing complete disbelief.\nIn conversation, it's often used to respond to someone's assumption, conveying "that's not possible" or "absolutely not."

结构：动词/形容词词干（无收音+ㄹ；有收音+을）+ 리가 없다。\\n리 = 道.en: Structure: Verb/Adjective stem (no batchim + ㄹ; with batchim + 을) + 리가 없다.\n리 = reason/logic (dependent noun), "there's no such logic" → "impossible."\nFor past speculation, use -았/었을 리가 없다.

和 -지 않을 것이다（不会）差别：\\n· -을 리가 없다：语气强烈，几乎断.en:
Difference from -지 않을 것이다 (won't):
· -을 리가 없다: Strong tone, almost asserting "absolutely impossible"
· 지 않을 것이다: Ordinary negative speculation, "probably won't"

In spoken language, -을 리가 있어요? (rhetorical: how could it be?) is commonly used and means the same as -을 리가 없다.

推测两极：说不定 vs 不可能.en: Two Extremes of Speculation: Maybe vs. Impossible

表达\"某种情况自然而然会发生\"的规律性判断。\\n带有\"这是天经地义\"的.en: Expresses a judgment that something naturally and inevitably happens.\nCarries the nuance of "it's only natural," often used to state universal truths or life patterns.\n-기 마련이다 and -게 마련이다 have exactly the same meaning and can be used interchangeably.

结构：动词/形容词词干 + 기 마련이다（或 -게 마련이다）。\\n마련이다.en: Structure: Verb/Adjective stem + 기 마련이다 (or -게 마련이다).\n마련이다 literally means "is prepared" → extended to "it's naturally like this."\nAttach directly to the stem regardless of the final consonant.

两个变体：\\n1. -기 마련이다：TOPIK 高频，日常也用\\n2. -게.en:
Two variants:
1. -기 마련이다: High frequency in TOPIK, also used in daily speech
2. -게 마련이다: Slightly more common in spoken language, with a slightly stronger nuance
The meaning is exactly the same—either one is correct.

Common usage: Often paired with words like 누구나 (anyone), 다들 (everyone) to emphasize universality.

表达\"某种情况很容易发生\"，通常指不好的结果。\\n和 -기 마련이다 结构.en: Expresses that "a certain situation easily happens," usually referring to a bad outcome.\nIt's structurally similar to -기 마련이다, but with a stronger and more negative tone.\nIt often appears in contexts of warning, advice, or concern.

结构：动词词干 + 기 십상이다。\\n십상 是汉字词\"十上\"，\"十次里有.en: Structure: Verb stem + 기 십상이다.\n십상 is a Sino-Korean word meaning "ten out of ten" → "nine times out of ten."\nIt mainly attaches to verbs and is used for the high probability of negative outcomes.

语感差别：\\n· -기 마련이다：中性，指普遍规律\\n· -기 십상이다：偏.en:
Nuance difference:
· -기 마련이다: Neutral, refers to a general rule
· -기 십상이다: Negative, refers to being prone to mistakes

Examples:
· 늙기 마련이다 (gets old) — objective rule
· 넘어지기 십상이다 (likely to fall) — warning

本来就……（道理规律）/ 从不…….en: It's only natural that... (by rule/logic) / Never...

-는 법이다 表达\"按道理/情理就是这样\"的规律。\\n-는 법이 없다 相.en: -는 법이다 expresses a rule that "by logic or common sense, this is how it is."\n-는 법이 없다 is the opposite, expressing a fixed negation meaning "this never happens."\nIt emphasizes "what should be" or "convention," leaning more toward moral/social rules than -기 마련이다.

结构：\\n· 动词词干 + 는 법이다（现在规律）\\n· 形容词词干（无收音.en:
Structure:
· Verb stem + 는 법이다 (present rule)
· Adjective stem (no batchim + ㄴ; with batchim + 은) + 법이다
· Noun + 인 법이다
Negation: -는 법이 없다 (never)

和 -기 마련이다 的选择：\\n· -기 마련이다：偏自然/生理规律\\n·.en:
Choosing between -기 마련이다 and -는 법이다:
· -기 마련이다: leans toward natural/physiological rules
· -는 법이다: leans toward social/logical rules
· They are often interchangeable, with the subtle difference being whether the focus is on "physiology" or "logic."

\"自然会/规律\"三大表达对照.en: Comparison of Three Expressions for "Naturally/By Rule"

显然是……（心里有数）.en: It's obviously... (you know it for sure)

表达\"根据情况判断，事情显然会是这样\"的强推测。\\n뻔하다 就是\"明摆着.en: Expresses a strong guess that "based on the situation, things will obviously turn out this way."\n뻔하다 means "clear, obvious, evident."\nIt carries a subjective judgment, with the speaker feeling very confident about the conclusion.

结构：\\n· 动词 + 는 게 뻔하다（现在/将来）\\n· 动词 + 은/ㄴ.en:
Structure:
· Verb + 는 게 뻔하다 (present/future)
· Verb + 은/ㄴ 게 뻔하다 (past)
· Adjective + 은/ㄴ 게 뻔하다
· Noun + 인 게 뻔하다

뻔하다 itself is an adjective meaning "obvious."

和 -을 리가 없다 相反：\\n· -을 리가 없다 = 断言\"不可能\"\.en:
Opposite of -을 리가 없다:
· -을 리가 없다 = asserting "impossible"
· -는 게 뻔하다 = asserting "obviously will"

Subtle difference from -을 게 틀림없다 (next lesson):
· -는 게 뻔하다 = inferred from the situation at hand
· -을 게 틀림없다 = inferred from evidence/rules

-는/은/ㄴ/을 게 뻔하다 · 冠形选择.en: -는/은/ㄴ/을 게 뻔하다 · Choosing the Adnominal Form

表达\"根据证据/规律，一定会……\"的最高确定性推测。\\n틀림없다 直译\".en: Expresses the highest level of certainty in a prediction, meaning "based on evidence/rules, it will definitely..."\n틀림없다 literally means "no mistake" → "certain and without doubt."\nIt is the opposite end of the spectrum from -을 리가 없다: one asserts "definitely yes," the other "definitely no."

结构：\\n· 动词/形容词 + 을/ㄹ 게 틀림없다（未来推测）\\n· 动词.en:
Structure:
· Verb/Adjective + 을/ㄹ 게 틀림없다 (future prediction)
· Past verb + 은/ㄴ 게 틀림없다 (past prediction)
· Noun + 인 게 틀림없다

틀림없다 can also be used alone, meaning "that's right."

推测确定性最高级：\\n· -을지도 모르다（20%）\\n· -을 것 같다（.en:
Highest level of certainty in predictions:
· -을지도 모르다 (20%)
· -을 것 같다 (60%)
· -을 것이다 (80%)
· -을 게 틀림없다 (95%) — this lesson

Similar to -는 게 뻔하다 but with a different nuance:
· 뻔하다: subjective judgment "you can tell at a glance"
· 틀림없다: objective evidence "based on rules"

完成这份练习，检验担忧、推测与规律八大语法。\\n覆盖：-을까 봐、-을지도 모.en: Complete this practice to test the eight grammar points covering worry, speculation, and rules.\nCovered: -을까 봐, -을지도 모르다, -을 리가 없다, -기 마련이다, -기 십상이다, -는 법이다, -는 게 뻔하다, -을 게 틀림없다.\nFocus on mastering the prediction certainty gradient and choosing the right rule-based grammar.

P22 八大语法分组：\\n【担忧】L01 -을까 봐\\n【推测】L02 -을.en:
P22 Eight Grammar Points Grouped:
【Worry】L01 -을까 봐
【Speculation】L02 -을지도 모르다 (might) · L03 -을 리가 없다 (impossible) · L07 -는 게 뻔하다 (obviously) · L08 -을 게 틀림없다 (definitely)
【Rules】L04 -기 마련이다 (natural rule) · L05 -기 십상이다 (negative warning) · L06 -는 법이다 (principle/rule)

综合练习 · 担忧、推测与规律.en: Comprehensive Practice · Worry, Speculation, and Patterns

与此相反……（对比两面）.en: On the other hand... (contrasting two sides)

表达同一件事物或情况的两个对立面。\\n\"一方面……另一方面……\"、\"…….en: Expresses two opposing aspects of the same thing or situation.\n"On one hand... on the other hand..." or "...while at the same time being the opposite..."\nIt emphasizes "two contrasting characteristics coexisting" more strongly than -지만 (although), and is a typical intermediate TOPIK contrast connector.

结构：\\n· 动词 + 는 반면에（现在）\\n· 动词 + 은/ㄴ 반면에（.en:
Structure:
· Verb + 는 반면에 (present)
· Verb + 은/ㄴ 반면에 (past)
· Adjective + 은/ㄴ 반면에
· Noun + 인 반면에

"에" can be omitted to form -는 반면, with no change in meaning.

和 -지만 差别：\\n· -지만：单纯转折\"虽然A但B\"\\n· -는 반.en:
Difference from -지만:
· -지만: simple contrast "although A, B"
· -는 반면에: emphasizes "A and B are opposing characteristics," usually two sides of the same subject.

Commonly used to analyze pros and cons or compare differences between two situations.

表达\"在A的基础上又加B\"的累加连接。\\n\"不仅……还……\"、\"又….en: Expresses an additive connection where "B is added on top of A."\n"Not only... but also..." or "both... and..."\nThe second clause usually goes further or deepens the degree compared to the first, and the tone is stronger than -고.

结构：\\n· 动词 + 는 데다가（现在）\\n· 动词过去 + 은/ㄴ 데다.en:
Structure:
· Verb + 는 데다가 (present)
· Verb past + 은/ㄴ 데다가
· Adjective + 은/ㄴ 데다가
· Noun + 인 데다가

"가" can be omitted to form -는 데다, with no change in meaning and a more formal tone.

和 -고 的差别：\\n· -고：单纯并列\"和/并且\"\\n· -는 데다가.en:
Difference from -고:
· -고: simple listing "and/also"
· -는 데다가: cumulative + intensifying, "even more..."

The second clause often includes intensifiers like -까지, -도, 더욱, emphasizing "going a step further".

强烈否定预期：\"别说 A，连 B 都不……\"或\"别说 A，反而 B\"。\.en: Strongly negates expectations: "Not to mention A, even B is not..." or "Not to mention A, rather B."\nExpresses that reality is far worse (or far different) than expected.\nThe tone is stronger than a general contrast, carrying disappointment or complaint.

结构：\\n· 动词/形容词词干 + 기는커녕 + 反预期结果\\n· 名词 +.en:
Structure:
· Verb/Adjective stem + 기는커녕 + unexpected result
· Noun + 은/는커녕 + unexpected result

The second clause often pairs with negative forms like -도 못하다 / -지도 않다, emphasizing "even the basic... is not...".

和 -는 반면에 差别：\\n· -는 반면에 = 客观对比\"A 与 B 相反.en:
Difference from -는 반면에:
· -는 반면에 = objective contrast "A is opposite to B"
· -기는커녕 = strong disappointment "Not to mention A, even B is not..."

Typical pattern:
· Expected to do A, but even B (which is lower than A) is not...
· "칭찬은커녕 혼났어요" (Not to mention praise, I got scolded)

和 -는 데다가 意思相似的书面表达。\\n\"不仅 A，而且 B\"，A 和.en: A written expression similar in meaning to -는 데다가.\n"Not only A, but also B," where A and B are accumulations of similar characteristics.\nMore commonly used in written language, formal speeches, and TOPIK writing.

结构：\\n· 动词/形容词无收音词干 + ㄹ뿐더러\\n· 动词/形容词有收音.en:
Structure:
· Verb/adjective stem without final consonant + ㄹ뿐더러
· Verb/adjective stem with final consonant + 을뿐더러
· Past tense + -았/었을뿐더러
· Noun + 일뿐더러

뿐더러 is a combination of "뿐" + "더러" and is written without a space.

和 -는 데다가 差别：\\n· -는 데다가：口语/日常都可，累加语气\\n·.en:
Difference from -는 데다가:
· -는 데다가: Can be used in both spoken and everyday language, with an additive tone
· -을뿐더러: More written/formal, with a more solemn tone

They can be used interchangeably; choose based on the situation. For TOPIK writing and company reports, -을뿐더러 is preferred.

书面累加连接词，\"不仅 A 也 B\"、\"既是 A 也是 B\"。\\n后半.en: A written additive connective, meaning "not only A but also B" or "both A and B."\nThe second clause often pairs with -도 to emphasize "also."\nMore literary, commonly found in TOPIK reading and news articles.

结构：\\n· 动词/形容词词干 + 거니와\\n· 过去 + -았/었거니와\.en:
Structure:
· Verb/adjective stem + 거니와
· Past tense + -았/었거니와
· Noun + 이거니와 / 거니와

Attach directly to the stem regardless of final consonant. For nouns, choose 이거니와 or 거니와 based on the presence of a final consonant.

和 -을뿐더러 差别：\\n· -을뿐더러：明确\"不仅……而且\"的累加\\n.en:
Difference from -을뿐더러:
· -을뿐더러: Clearly indicates "not only... but also..." with an additive nuance
· -거니와: Presents a parallel of "both A and B," with a more balanced feel

Both are written-oriented, but -거니와 feels closer to the formal "and/also," while -을뿐더러 feels closer to "moreover."

一方面……另一方面…….en: On one hand... on the other hand...

连接同一时段发生的两件平行的事情或情况。\\n\"一方面 A，另一方面 B\"，.en: Connects two parallel events or situations that occur at the same time.\n"On one hand A, on the other hand B" — the two events are often actions or states of the same subject.\nUsed to describe complex situations, multifaceted aspects, or activities happening in parallel.

结构：\\n· 动词 + 는 한편（现在）\\n· 动词过去 + 은/ㄴ 한편\.en:
Structure:
· Verb + 는 한편 (present)
· Verb past + 은/ㄴ 한편
· Adjective + 은/ㄴ 한편
· Noun + 인 한편

한편 is itself a noun meaning "one side/one aspect," and it forms a connective phrase when combined with an adnominal ending.

和 -는 반면에 差别：\\n· -는 반면에：强调\"对立\"（A ↔ B）\.en:
Difference from -는 반면에:
· -는 반면에: emphasizes "contrast" (A ↔ B)
· -는 한편: emphasizes "parallelism" (A + B coexist)

Typical pattern: state one aspect of a subject (A) + simultaneously another aspect (B).

连接前后矛盾/意外的事件：\"做了 A 却 B\"、\"是 A 却 B\"。\\.en: Connects contradictory or unexpected events: "did A yet B," "is A yet B."\nThe two events involve the same subject, creating an "unexpected contrast."\nSimilar to -지만 but places stronger emphasis on "the event already happened yet the result is surprising."

结构：动词/形容词词干 + 고도。\\n不看收音，所有词类同一接法。\\n形容词.en: Structure: verb/adjective stem + 고도.\nRegardless of the final consonant, all word types take the same ending.\nAdjectives are used less frequently; it most commonly combines with verbs.

典型套路：\\n· 前半：动作/状态已完成\\n· 后半：出人意料的反面结果\\.en:
Typical pattern:
· First half: action/state is completed
· Second half: unexpected opposite result

Difference from -고:
· -고: coordination/sequence "did A then B"
· -고도: unexpected contrast "did A yet B"

Difference from -지만: stronger tone, with more emphasis on "event + contrast."

\"뿐\" 表\"仅\"，\"아니라\"表\"不是\" → \"不仅仅是 A\".en: "뿐" means "only," and "아니라" means "not" → "not just A" → followed by more.\nWorks in both spoken and written language, making it the most balanced additive connector.\nIt's nearly identical in meaning to -을뿐더러, but more neutral and more common.

结构：\\n· 动词/形容词无收音 + ㄹ 뿐 아니라\\n· 动词/形容词有收.en:
Structure:
· Verb/Adjective without batchim + ㄹ 뿐 아니라
· Verb/Adjective with batchim + 을 뿐 아니라
· Past tense + -았/었을 뿐 아니라
· Noun + 뿐 아니라 (directly attached) / Noun + 일 뿐 아니라 (using -이다)

뿐 can be written with a space after it, or as -을뿐 아니라 (in some textbooks).

累加连接词 대비:\\n· -고: 单纯并列（口语）\\n· -는 데다가: 累.en:
Additive connectors comparison:
· -고: simple listing (spoken)
· -는 데다가: additive emphasis (spoken/daily)
· -을 뿐 아니라: general additive (spoken/written)
· -을뿐더러: written additive (formal)
· -거니와: literary additive

-을 뿐 아니라 is the most practical and neutral. It's common across all TOPIK levels.

完成这份练习，检验高级连接与对比八大语法。\\n覆盖：-는 반면에、-는 데다가.en: Complete this practice to test your mastery of eight advanced connectors and contrast grammar points.\nCovers: -는 반면에, -는 데다가, -기는커녕, -을뿐더러, -거니와, -는 한편, -고도, -을 뿐 아니라.\nFocus on distinguishing the four relationships: contrast / addition / reversal / parallel.

P23 语法分组：\\n【对立】L01 -는 반면에\\n【累加】L02 -는.en:
P23 Grammar Grouping:
[Contrast] L01 -는 반면에
[Accumulation] L02 -는 데다가 · L04 -을뿐더러 · L05 -거니와 · L08 -을 뿐 아니라
[Reversal] L03 -기는커녕 · L07 -고도
[Parallel] L06 -는 한편

综合练习 · 高级连接与对比.en: Comprehensive Practice · Advanced Connections and Contrasts

因为（意外原因）导致…….en: Because of (an unexpected cause) leading to...

表达\"因为某个意外/突发情况，结果出了岔子\"的原因连接词。\\n后半句通常是.en:
A connective expressing "because of an unexpected/sudden situation, things went wrong."
The second clause is usually a negative/unexpected result.
Unlike regular -아/어서 or -기 때문에, 바람에 emphasizes "an unforeseen cause leading to an unforeseen result."

结构：动词词干 + 는 바람에。\\n只接动词，不接形容词、不接名词。\\n결과.en:
Structure: verb stem + 는 바람에.
Only attaches to verbs, not adjectives or nouns.
The result (second clause) must be in the past tense.
바람 is a noun meaning "wind/momentum," extended to mean "(sudden) force."

关键限制：\\n1. 前半句只能是动词，不能是形容词\\n2. 后半句必须是过去.en:
Key restrictions:
1. The first clause can only be a verb, not an adjective
2. The second clause must be past tense (-았/었어요)
3. The second clause is usually a negative/unexpected result
4. The subjects of the two clauses can differ

Difference from -기 때문에: objective reason vs. unexpected sudden event.

和 -는 바람에 相似，但 -는 통에 语气更强，强调\"因为混乱/干扰的场面\.en:
Similar to -는 바람에, but -는 통에 has a stronger tone, emphasizing that the consequence results from "a chaotic/disruptive scene."
The character "통" implies a "noisy, messy" situation.
Commonly used in contexts with many people, loud noise, or complex events.

结构：动词词干 + 는 통에；表混乱状态的形容词 + 은 통에（如 많은 통에、.en: Structure: verb stem + 는 통에; adjectives describing chaotic states + 은 통에 (e.g., 많은 통에, 시끄러운 통에).\nThe latter part is usually in past tense with a negative result.\nDifference: 바람에 emphasizes "suddenness," while 통에 emphasizes "chaos/interference."

典型场景：\\n1. 人多闹哄哄（사람이 많은 통에）\\n2. 打闹分心（싸우.en:
Typical scenarios:
1. Crowded and noisy (사람이 많은 통에)
2. Distracted by fighting (싸우는 통에)
3. Interrupted by an event (전화 오는 통에)

It can often be swapped with -는 바람에, but 통에 has a stronger tone and is more commonly used for negative complaints.

因为……的错（归咎负面）.en: Because of... (attributing blame for negative outcomes)

带\"归咎/责怪\"意味的原因表达。\\n\"都怪 A，才 B\"，语气是把不好.en: An expression of cause with a sense of "blame/attribution."\n"It's all A's fault that B happened," with a tone that blames the bad result on A.\nIt is the exact opposite of -는 덕분에 (thanks to).

结构：\\n· 动词现在 + 는 탓에\\n· 动词过去/形容词 + 은/ㄴ 탓.en:
Structure:
· Verb present + 는 탓에
· Verb past / adjective + 은/ㄴ 탓에
· Noun + 탓에 (directly attached)

탓 itself is a noun meaning "responsibility, fault."

关键差别：\\n· -는 바람에：意外突发（不带责怪）\\n· -는 통에：混乱.en:
Key differences:
· -는 바람에: unexpected sudden event (no blame)
· -는 통에: chaotic interference (complaint)
· -는 탓에: explicit blame ("it's all...'s fault")

It is the opposite pair of -는 덕분에:
· Good result → 덕분에 (thanks to)
· Bad result → 탓에 (blame on)

탓 vs 덕분：归咎与感激.en: 탓 vs 덕분: Blame vs Gratitude

多亏 vs 都怪.en: Thanks to vs Blame it on

这一课把两个\"归因型\"连接词彻底分开。\\n덕분에：多亏 · 感恩 · 后半.en:
This lesson clearly separates two "attribution-type" connectors.
덕분에: thanks to · grateful · the second clause must be a positive result.
탓에: blame it on · fault · the second clause must be a negative result.
In everyday Korean, these two are strictly distinguished—using the wrong one can sound rude or flip the meaning.

덕분에 结构：\\n动词现在 → -는 덕분에\\n动词过去/形容词 → -은/.en:
덕분에 structure:
Verb present → -는 덕분에
Verb past/Adjective → -은/ㄴ 덕분에
Noun → (이)ㄴ 덕분에 / noun 덕분에

탓에 has a parallel structure, but the second clause must be negative.

判断口诀：\\n1. 结果好 → 덕분에（好事归功）\\n2. 结果坏 → 탓에.en:
Quick guide:
1. Good result → 덕분에 (credit the good thing)
2. Bad result → 탓에 (blame the bad thing)
3. Neutral statement → use -기 때문에
4. Unexpected/sudden → use -는 바람에

덕분에 can also stand alone as an adverb: "덕분에 잘 지내요" (thanks to you, I'm doing well).

表达\"因为极端的情绪/状态，做出了通常不会做的事\"。\\n\"나머지\"本意.en: Expresses "because of an extreme emotion/state, you did something you normally wouldn't do."\n"나머지" literally means "the remaining part," but grammatically it conveys "emotion overflowing—the leftover part leads to the consequence."\nUsed in written language, novels, and news; rarely in speech.

结构：\\n动词/形容词现在 → -는 나머지\\n动词过去 → -은/ㄴ 나머.en:
Structure:
Verb/Adjective present → -는 나머지
Verb past → -은/ㄴ 나머지
Adjective past → -았/었던 나머지
The second clause must be in past tense (expressing an actual result).

关键点：\\n1. 前半通常是强烈的情绪或状态（긴장, 놀라, 화가 나, 기쁘.en:
Key points:
1. The first part is usually a strong emotion or state (긴장, 놀라, 화가 나, 기쁘, 슬프)
2. The second part is an "extreme reaction" (쓰러지다, 소리를 지르다, 말을 못 하다)
3. Strongly written; in speech, use -어서 or 너무 -아서
4. Cannot be used with future tense or imperative sentences

나머지 前项形态.en: Forms of the Preceding Clause for 나머지

\"관계로\"是原因连接词的公文体、书面体。\\n意思等同于 -기 때문에，但语.en: "관계로" is a formal, written-style connective for expressing reasons.\nIts meaning is equivalent to -기 때문에, but the tone is more formal and objective.\nIt is commonly used in notices, announcements, news, and explanatory texts to state objective, unchangeable reasons.

结构：\\n动词现在 → -는 관계로\\n动词过去/形容词 → -은/ㄴ 관계.en:
Structure:
Verb (present) → -는 관계로
Verb (past) / Adjective → -은/ㄴ 관계로
Noun → -인 관계로 / 명사 관계로

"관계" literally means "relation," and after grammaticalization, it expresses "due to the relation of...".

使用要点：\\n1. 只用于书面/正式场合（公告、通知、公文、演讲）\\n2..en:
Usage points:
1. Used only in written/formal settings (announcements, notices, official documents, speeches)
2. In spoken language, use -기 때문에 or -아/어서
3. The latter part is usually an objective decision or result (휴무, 취소, 연기, 종료)
4. It carries no emotional nuance and is very objective

관계로 前项接续.en: Connecting the Preceding Clause with 관계로

趁着·借机顺便.en: While at it / Taking the opportunity to

\"김\"字面意为\"势头/正在做的事的势头\"。\\n表达\"既然正在做某事（.en: "김" literally means "momentum" or "the momentum of what you're doing."\nIt expresses "since you're already doing something (or have done it), take this opportunity to do another thing as well."\nThe latter part is usually an additional action done conveniently.

结构：\\n动词现在 → -는 김에\\n动词过去 → -은/ㄴ 김에\\n只接.en:
Structure:
Verb (present) → -는 김에
Verb (past) → -은/ㄴ 김에
Only attaches to verbs, not adjectives or nouns.
There is no tense restriction on the latter clause.

要点：\\n1. 前半必须是动作（动词），主语与后半通常一致\\n2. 前后两个.en:
Key points:
1. The first part must be an action (verb), and the subject usually matches the second part
2. The two actions should be related (cannot be completely unrelated)
3. Often used with "오다/가다/하다/사다/만나다"
4. Meaning: "take the opportunity to do something related"

这一课把本章学到的所有\"原因\"型连接词汇总起来做区分。\\n共 5 个高频候.en:
This lesson summarizes and distinguishes all the "cause" type connectors learned in this chapter.
There are 5 high-frequency candidates: -기 때문에 / -아서 / -는 바람에 / -는 통에 / -는 탓에.
Choose the correct one based on three dimensions: meaning, nuance, and restrictions on the second clause.

五连接词接续总览：\\n-기 때문에：动词+기 / 形容词+기 / 名词+이기\.en:
Overview of the five connectors:
-기 때문에: verb + 기 / adjective + 기 / noun + 이기
-아/어서: verb or adjective based on ㅏㅗ/other
-는 바람에: only attaches to verbs in present adnominal form
-는 통에: only attaches to verbs in present adnominal form
-는/은 탓에: verb present -는 / verb past·adjective -은/ㄴ / noun 탓에

选择判断树：\\n1. 是不是客观陈述？→ -기 때문에 / -아서\\n2..en:
Decision tree for choosing:
1. Is it an objective statement? → -기 때문에 / -아서
2. Is the result unexpected/sudden? → -는 바람에
3. Is it chaos/noise causing the speaker to suffer? → -는 통에
4. Is it negative + blame? → -는 탓에
5. Is it positive gratitude? → -는 덕분에

五大原因连接词一览.en: Overview of the Five Cause Connectors

「-길래」表示\"因为观察到某情境（或听到某消息），所以做了某事\"。主语常是\.en: 「-길래」means "because I observed a situation (or heard news), I did something." The subject is often "I" (first person); the first clause is a directly observed/heard situation, and the second clause is "my" reaction. The tone is colloquial, on a different level from the written form -기에.

动词/形容词词干 + -길래｜前句：观察/所闻｜后句：说话人的反应.en: Verb/Adjective stem + -길래 ｜ First clause: observation/heard news ｜ Second clause: speaker's reaction

不看收音（词干直接加）｜主语常为第一人称｜前句多为直接看到/听到；书面用 -기에.en: No batchim check (attach directly to stem) ｜ Subject is often first person ｜ First clause is usually something directly seen/heard; written form uses -기에

完成这份练习，检验高级原因表达八大语法。\\n覆盖：-는 바람에、-는 통에、-.en: Complete this practice to test the eight advanced cause-and-effect expressions.\nCovers: -는 바람에, -는 통에, -는 탓에, -는 덕분에, -는 나머지, -는 관계로, -는 김에, and a comprehensive comparison of cause connectors.\nFocus on mastering six types of cause-and-effect relationships: "unexpected/sudden, chaotic/suffering, blame/negative, gratitude/positive, extreme emotion, announcement style, and doing something while at it."

P24 语法分组：\\n【意外突发】L01 -는 바람에\\n【混乱受苦】L02.en:
P24 Grammar Grouping:
【Unexpected/Sudden】L01 -는 바람에
【Chaos/Suffering】L02 -는 통에
【Blame/Negative】L03 -는/은 탓에
【Gratitude/Positive】L04 -는 덕분에
【Extreme Emotion】L05 -는/은 나머지
【Announcement Style】L06 -는 관계로
【Doing While At It】L07 -는 김에
【Comprehensive Comparison】L08 Five Cause Connectors Compared

把别人的原话转述给第三者，就是\"间接引用\"。\\n韩语间接引用比中文更严格：.en: To relay someone else's original words to a third person is called "indirect quotation."\nKorean indirect quotation is stricter than in Chinese: verbs, adjectives, and nouns each have their own forms.\nThis lesson explains the four basic forms of indirect quotation for declarative sentences all at once.

陈述句间接引用结构：\\n动词现在（有收音）→ -는다고 하다\\n动词现在（无.en:
Declarative indirect quotation structure:
Verb present (with final consonant) → -는다고 하다
Verb present (no final consonant) → -ㄴ다고 하다
Verb past → -았/었다고 하다
Adjective → -다고 하다
Noun → -(이)라고 하다

核心规则：\\n1. 直接引语的敬语级要\"脱下\"再\"重穿\" → 하다 层.en:
Core rules:
1. The politeness level of the direct quote must be "taken off" and "put back on" → determined by the level of 하다
2. Tense is marked on the verb/adjective, not on 하다
3. Nouns use -(이)라고, not -다고
4. 하다 can change → 그러다 / 그랬다 / 물어보다, etc.

把别人的问句转述给第三者，用 -냐고 하다 / -느냐고 하다。\\n\"你要不.en: To relay someone else's question to a third person, use -냐고 하다 / -느냐고 하다.\n"Are you coming?" → 그가 오냐고 물었어요.\nIn spoken Korean, both verbs and adjectives can directly use -냐고; in written Korean, the more formal rules distinguish between them.

结构（口语通用）：\\n动词/形容词现在 → -냐고 하다\\n动词/形容词过去.en:
Structure (common in speech):
Verb/Adjective present → -냐고 하다
Verb/Adjective past → -았/었냐고 하다
Noun → -(이)냐고 하다

Formal written version: Verb -느냐고, Adjective -(으)냐고.

要点：\\n1. 하다 可以换 물어보다 / 궁금해하다 表\"问/好奇\"\\.en:
Key points:
1. 하다 can be replaced with 물어보다 / 궁금해하다 to mean "ask/wonder"
2. Question words (뭐, 언제, 어디, 왜) can be inserted in the middle
3. Shortened form: -냬 (-냐고 해 → -냬)
4. After nouns, you must use -(이)냐고, not -냐고

疑问句间接引用总表.en: Summary Table: Indirect Quotation of Questions

把别人的\"我们一起……吧\"这种共动/建议句转述给第三者，用 -자고 하다。\.en: Use -자고 하다 to relay someone else's suggestion or proposal ("Let's... together") to a third person.\n"같이 밥 먹자." → 친구가 같이 밥 먹자고 했어요.\nIt only attaches to verbs, not adjectives or nouns.

结构：\\n动词现在 → -자고 하다\\n否定 → -지 말자고 하다\\n名.en:
Structure:
Verb (present) → -자고 하다
Negative → -지 말자고 하다
Noun × / Adjective × (cannot be used)

하다 can be replaced with 제안하다 / 권하다.

要点：\\n1. 只接动词，且必须是共同动作（一起做的动作）\\n2. 说话人和.en:
Key points:
1. Only attaches to verbs, and the action must be a joint action (done together)
2. Both the speaker and the listener can be the doers
3. Negative uses -지 말자고 하다 ("Let's not...")
4. Contracted form: -쟤 (-자고 해 → -쟤)

把命令句\"你去做！\"转述给第三者，用 -(으)라고 하다。\\n\"빨리 와.en: Use -(으)라고 하다 to relay a command ("You do it!") to a third person.\n"빨리 와!" → 엄마가 빨리 오라고 하셨어요.\nIt only attaches to verbs, and the doer is the listener (not the speaker).

结构：\\n动词有收音 → -으라고 하다\\n动词无收音 → -라고 하다\\.en:
Structure:
Verb with final consonant → -으라고 하다
Verb without final consonant → -라고 하다
Negative → -지 말라고 하다

Noun × / Adjective × (commands don't take nouns or adjectives)

要点：\\n1. 只接动词，执行者是听话人\\n2. 有收音加 -으라고，无收音.en:
Key points:
1. Only attaches to verbs, and the doer is the listener
2. Add -으라고 after a final consonant, -라고 after no final consonant
3. Negative uses -지 말라고 하다 ("Don't do...")
4. Special verb 주다 → 달라고 하다 (asking for oneself) / 주라고 하다 (asking for someone else)

别人说的话成为\"我做某事\"的依据，用 -다고 해서 或 -는다길래。\\n\.en: When someone else's words become the reason for "what I did," use -다고 해서 or -는다길래.\n"I heard that café is famous, so I went."\n-다고 해서 is neutral and general, while -는다길래 is more colloquial and vivid.

结构：\\n动词现在 → -는다고 해서 / -는다길래（无收音 -ㄴ다길래）\.en:
Structure:
Verb present → -는다고 해서 / -는다길래 (no batchim: -ㄴ다길래)
Verb past → -았/었다고 해서 / -았/었다길래
Adjective → -다고 해서 / -다길래
Noun → -(이)라고 해서 / -(이)라길래

要点：\\n1. 前项是\"听/得知\"的内容，后项是自己的反应\\n2. -다.en:
Key points:
1. The first clause is what you "heard/learned," and the second clause is your reaction
2. -다고 해서: written/neutral; -는다길래: colloquial/emotional
3. With -는다길래, the subjects of the two clauses must be different (the one who heard and the one who acted are not the same person)
4. The second clause often expresses surprise/reason/reaction

把听到的传闻拿去向本人或他人求证，用 -다면서? / -다면서요?。\\n\"听.en: Use -다면서? / -다면서요? to confirm something you heard with the person involved or with others.\n"I heard you got into college?" → 대학교 합격했다면서요?\nIt carries a tone of surprise/excitement/confirmation.

结构（问句·带 ? 号）：\\n动词现在 → -는다면서?/ㄴ다면서?\\n动词.en:
Structure (questions with ?):
Verb present → -는다면서?/ㄴ다면서?
Verb past → -았/었다면서?
Adjective → -다면서?
Noun → -(이)라면서?

Add -요 for polite form: -다면서요?

要点：\\n1. 语气：既有\"确认\"又有\"惊喜/意外\"\\n2. 只用于.en:
Key points:
1. Tone: combines "confirmation" with "surprise/unexpectedness"
2. Used only in questions (with ?)
3. Generally use -다면서요? instead of -다면서? (when showing respect)
4. In conversation, shortened to -다며? / -다며요?

「-다니 / -다니요」用于对听到的事实表示惊讶、感叹、意外或不敢相信，中文常译.en: 「-다니 / -다니요」 is used to express surprise, exclamation, unexpectedness, or disbelief about something you've heard. It can be translated as "to think that..." "how could..." or "no way..." in English. It is a shortened form of the indirect quotation -다고 하다.

动词现在 -는/ㄴ다니 · 动词过去 -았/었다니 · 形容词 -다니 · 名词.en: Verb present -는/ㄴ다니 · Verb past -았/었다니 · Adjective -다니 · Noun -(이)라니. Add "요" for polite form: -다니요

动词现在（有收音）→ -는다니；动词现在（无收音）→ -ㄴ다니；动词过去 → -.en: Verb present (with final consonant) → -는다니; Verb present (no final consonant) → -ㄴ다니; Verb past → -았/었다니; Adjective → -다니; Noun (with final consonant) → -이라니, (no final consonant) → -라니

「-다는 / -는다는 / -ㄴ다는 / -(이)라는」是间接引用 -다고 하다.en: 「-다는 / -는다는 / -ㄴ다는 / -(이)라는」 is the adnominal form of the indirect quotation -다고 하다, turning "saying..." into a modifier for a noun. In Chinese, it corresponds to "the (news/rumor/fact) that says...". It is a high-frequency structure in news and written language.

动词现在（有收音）-는다는 / 动词现在（无收音）-ㄴ다는 / 动词过去 -았/.en: Verb present (with final consonant) -는다는 / Verb present (no final consonant) -ㄴ다는 / Verb past -았/었다는 / Adjective -다는 / Noun -(이)라는

这是 -다고 하는 的省略。核心公式：现在 -는/ㄴ다는 · 过去 -았/었다는.en: This is a shortened form of -다고 하는. Core formula: Present -는/ㄴ다는 · Past -았/었다는 · Adjective -다는 · Noun -(이)라는. Followed by nouns such as 소식/이야기/사실/소문/생각

本练习综合复习 P25 高级引用与转述章节的 8 个语法点，帮助巩固间接引用的完.en: This exercise comprehensively reviews the 8 grammar points from the P25 Advanced Quotation and Reported Speech chapter, helping to solidify the complete system of indirect quotation.

综合本 Part 所有语法.en: Comprehensive review of all grammar points in this Part

重点在识别不同引用形式的使用场景.en: Focus on identifying the usage contexts of different quotation forms

「-더라도」表示强让步，\"就算……也……\"\"即使……也……\"。用于假设的.en: 「-더라도」 expresses strong concession, meaning "even if..." or "even though...". It is used for hypothetical situations, emphasizing that regardless of the premise, the following action/state remains unchanged. The tone is stronger and more formal than -아/어도.

直接连接词干，不看收音；过去 -았/었더라도；名词用 -(이)라 하더라도.en: Attach directly to the stem regardless of final consonant; past tense -았/었더라도; for nouns use -(이)라 하더라도

「-을/ㄹ지라도」是最书面、最强的让步表达，\"即使……也……\"\"纵然……也.en: 「-을/ㄹ지라도」 is the most formal and strongest concessive expression, meaning "even if..." or "even though...". It is commonly used in literature, speeches, and formal writing. Its nuance is more classical and formal than -더라도.

动词/形容词词干：有收音 + -을지라도 / 无收音 + -ㄹ지라도 · 名词.en: Verb/Adjective stem: with final consonant + -을지라도 / without final consonant + -ㄹ지라도 · Noun + -(이)ㄹ지라도

受收音影响：有收音 -을지라도，无收音 -ㄹ지라도；过去 -았/었을지라도；名词.en: Affected by final consonant: with final consonant -을지라도, without final consonant -ㄹ지라도; past tense -았/었을지라도; for nouns use -(이)ㄹ지라도

「-을/ㄹ지언정」表达强烈的\"宁可A也不B\"\"哪怕A也不做B\"，前句是宁.en: 「-을/ㄹ지언정」 expresses a strong sense of "rather A than B" or "even if A, never B." The first clause presents a negative situation one is willing to accept, while the second clause states something one absolutely refuses to do. The tone is very firm and formal, commonly found in written language.

词干：有收音 + -을지언정 / 无收音 + -ㄹ지언정 · 名词 -(이)ㄹ지.en: Verb stem: with final consonant + -을지언정 / without final consonant + -ㄹ지언정 · Noun + -(이)ㄹ지언정

与 -을/ㄹ지라도 结构相同，但语义不同：前者纯让步\"纵然\"，后者带对比\".en: It has the same structure as -을/ㄹ지라도, but the meaning differs: the former is purely concessive ("even if"), while the latter carries contrast ("rather").

「-을/ㄹ망정」表达\"就算……也……\"\"哪怕……也……\"，含有\"退一步.en: 「-을/ㄹ망정」 expresses "even if... still..." or "even if... at least...", carrying a nuance of "conceding a step, but the bottom line remains unchanged." The first clause is a minimal concession, while the second clause emphasizes a boundary that cannot be crossed.

词干：有收音 -을망정 / 无收音 -ㄹ망정 · 名词 -(이)ㄹ망정.en: Verb stem: with final consonant -을망정 / without final consonant -ㄹ망정 · Noun + -(이)ㄹ망정

结构类似 -을지언정，但语气比 -을지언정 稍弱，更常用；后句常为消极/否定/义.en: The structure is similar to -을지언정, but the tone is slightly weaker and more commonly used; the following clause often expresses a negative, negative, or obligatory meaning.

即便到……的地步.en: Even if it comes to the point of...

「-는 한이 있어도 / -는 한이 있더라도」表示\"即便到了……的地步也…….en: 「-는 한이 있어도 / -는 한이 있더라도」means "even if it comes to the point of..." The preceding clause presents the most extreme/worst outcome, and the following clause expresses a firm determination. The tone is strong and is mainly used in written language and firm statements.

动词词干 + -는 한이 있어도 / -는 한이 있더라도.en: Verb stem + -는 한이 있어도 / -는 한이 있더라도

固定搭配 \"N + 한이 있어도\" 或直接接动词 -는 한이 있어도；名词用.en: Fixed expression "N + 한이 있어도" or directly attach to verbs as -는 한이 있어도; for nouns, use -(이)라는 한이 있어도

「-고자 / -고자 하다」表示意图、目的、打算，\"想……\"\"打算……\".en: 「-고자 / -고자 하다」 expresses intention, purpose, or plan, meaning "want to..." "plan to..." "in order to...". The tone is formal and is mainly used in written language, speeches, news, and official documents. It is the formal equivalent of the colloquial -(으)려고 / -(으)려고 하다.

动词词干 + -고자（连接） · 动词词干 + -고자 하다（做谓语）.en: Verb stem + -고자 (connective) · Verb stem + -고자 하다 (as predicate)

主语必须一致；不与形容词/名词连用；-고자 直接接词干，不看收音.en: The subject must be consistent; cannot be used with adjectives or nouns; -고자 attaches directly to the stem regardless of the final consonant.

「-도록」有多义：① 目的\"为了……\"\"让……\"，② 程度\"到……地步.en: 「-도록」 has multiple meanings: ① purpose "in order to..." "so that...", ② degree "to the point of...", ③ euphemistic command/suggestion (-도록 하다). The core meaning is "to lead to a certain result or state".

动词/形容词词干 + -도록（不看收音） · -도록 하다 委婉命令.en: Verb/Adjective stem + -도록 (regardless of final consonant) · -도록 하다 for euphemistic commands

语义1：目的（다치지 않도록）；语义2：程度（밤이 새도록）；语义3：委婉命令（.en: Meaning 1: purpose (다치지 않도록); Meaning 2: degree (밤이 새도록); Meaning 3: euphemistic command (시간을 지키도록 하세요)

「N + 치고」有两种用法：① 全称\"说到……没有例外/都是……\"，② 例外.en: 「N + 치고」has two usages: ① Universal statement "Speaking of..., there is no exception / all are...", ② Exception or concessive "As for..., (surprisingly)...". The meaning is determined by context.

名词 + 치고 · 常见搭配 \"N 치고 -지 않은/없는 것이 없다\"（全.en: Noun + 치고 · Common collocations "N 치고 -지 않은/없는 것이 없다" (universal) or "N 치고 unexpected result" (exception)

语义1 全称：后接双否定\"没有不……的\"；语义2 例外：后接与常识相反的结果.en: Meaning 1 (universal): followed by double negation "there is none that is not..."; Meaning 2 (exception): followed by a result contrary to common sense

本练习综合复习 P26 让步与意图强化章节的 8 个语法点：-더라도、-을/ㄹ지.en: This exercise comprehensively reviews the 8 grammar points from the P26 concession and intention reinforcement chapter: -더라도, -을/ㄹ지라도, -을/ㄹ지언정, -을/ㄹ망정, -는 한이 있어도, -고자, -도록, -치고.

重点在让步语气强度阶梯和意图/目的三种表达的辨析.en: Focus on the intensity hierarchy of concessive tones and the distinction among the three expressions of intention/purpose

「-기 마련이다」表示\"本来就……\"\"必然会……\"\"理所当然……\"。.en: '-기 마련이다' means "it's only natural that..." "it's bound to..." "it's理所当然 that...". It is used to state universal rules, common sense, or inevitable results. The tone is relatively objective and is often used in moralizing or summarizing experiences.

动词/形容词词干 + -기 마련이다 · 名词 + 이기 마련이다.en: Verb/Adjective stem + -기 마련이다 · Noun + 이기 마련이다

直接接词干，不看收音；名词加系词 이 后再接；等同 -는 법이다.en: Attach directly to the stem regardless of the final consonant; for nouns, add the copula 이 first; equivalent to -는 법이다

「-는 법이다 / -은/ㄴ 법이다」表示\"本来就……\"\"按道理讲……\".en: '-는 법이다 / -은/ㄴ 법이다' means "it's only natural that..." "by all logic..." "naturally...". It is used to state universal rules or principles, with a more literary tone and a moralizing/warning nuance. It is also commonly used in the form -는 법이 없다 to mean "will never..."

动词现在 -는 법이다 · 形容词 -은/ㄴ 법이다 · 名词 -인 법이다 ·.en: Verb present -는 법이다 · Adjective -은/ㄴ 법이다 · Noun -인 법이다 · Negative -는 법이 없다

动词冠形 -는，形容词冠形 -은/ㄴ；否定用 -는 법이 없다 表强烈否认.en: Use the adnominal form -는 for verbs and -은/ㄴ for adjectives; the negative form -는 법이 없다 expresses strong denial

「-을/ㄹ 법하다」表示\"看起来会……\"\"有可能……\"\"大概会……\".en: 「-을/ㄹ 법하다」 expresses "it looks like..." "it's possible that..." "it probably will...". It is used to make a guess about a possibility, with a slightly literary and formal tone. It is similar to -을/ㄹ 것 같다, but more euphemistic and classical.

动词/形容词词干：有收音 -을 법하다 / 无收音 -ㄹ 법하다 · 名词 -(.en: Verb/Adjective stem: with final consonant -을 법하다 / without final consonant -ㄹ 법하다 · Noun -(이)ㄹ 법하다

与 -는 법이다 结构相近但语义不同！-는 법이다 = 必然道理；-을/ㄹ 법하.en: It is structurally similar to -는 법이다 but semantically different! -는 법이다 = inevitable rule; -을/ㄹ 법하다 = possible. Pay special attention to distinguish them.

「-기 나름이다」表示\"取决于……的方式/程度\"\"看你怎么……\"。前接动.en: 「-기 나름이다」 means "it depends on how..." or "it's up to how you...". It is attached to a verb to express that the result depends on that action or method. The noun version is "N 나름이다" (depends on N).

动词接 -기 后 + 나름이다；名词直接 + 나름이다；不与形容词连用.en: Attach -기 to a verb stem, then add 나름이다; attach directly to a noun; not used with adjectives.

「-기에 달려 있다」表示\"取决于……\"\"在于……\"\"看……\"。用于.en: '-기에 달려 있다' means 'depends on...', 'lies in...', or 'is up to...'. It is used to emphasize the key determining factor of a situation. The noun version is 'N에 달려 있다'. Its tone is more formal and written than -기 나름이다.

动词词干 + -기에 달려 있다 · 名词 + 에 달려 있다.en: Verb stem + -기에 달려 있다 · Noun + 에 달려 있다

固定搭配\"-기에 달려 있다\"；主语常为决定的对象（성공/실패/미래 等）.en: Fixed expression '-기에 달려 있다'; the subject is often the thing being determined (e.g., 성공/실패/미래).

「-는/은/ㄴ 셈이다」表示\"算是……\"\"相当于……\"\"可以说是……\.en: The expression '-는/은/ㄴ 셈이다' means "it counts as...", "it is equivalent to...", or "it can be said that...". It is used to make an estimation or evaluation after considering various aspects. It is often used in conclusions drawn from summarizing, assessing, or comparing.

动词现在 -는 셈이다 · 形容词 -은/ㄴ 셈이다 · 名词 -인 셈이다 ·.en: Verb present: -는 셈이다 · Adjective: -은/ㄴ 셈이다 · Noun: -인 셈이다 · Past: -은/ㄴ 셈이다

关注冠形选择：动词现在 -는，动词过去 -은/ㄴ，形容词 -은/ㄴ，名词 -인.en: Pay attention to the adnominal form selection: verb present -는, verb past -은/ㄴ, adjective -은/ㄴ, noun -인

「-는/은/ㄴ 셈치다」表示\"就当作……\"\"假设……\"\"视为……\"。.en: The expression '-는/은/ㄴ 셈치다' means "just consider it as...", "suppose that...", or "regard it as...". It is used for hypothetical situations, mental concessions, or comforting oneself to accept a certain situation. The tone is similar to "let's pretend it didn't happen".

动词现在 -는 셈치다 · 动词过去 -은/ㄴ 셈치다 · 形容词 -은/ㄴ 셈.en: Verb present: -는 셈치다 · Verb past: -은/ㄴ 셈치다 · Adjective: -은/ㄴ 셈치다 · Noun: -인 셈치다

常搭配 -고 用作连接：\"-는 셈치고\" = 就当作……，然后…….en: Often used with -고 as a connective: "-는 셈치고" = just consider it as..., and then...

「-는/은/ㄴ 척하다 / -는/은/ㄴ 체하다」表示\"假装……\"\"装作….en: 「-는/은/ㄴ 척하다 / -는/은/ㄴ 체하다」 means "to pretend..." or "to act as if...". The two forms are nearly identical in meaning, with 척하다 being more colloquial and 체하다 more formal. The adnominal (modifier) form changes depending on the part of speech, just like with -셈이다.

动词现在 -는 척하다 · 动词过去 -은/ㄴ 척하다 · 形容词 -은/ㄴ 척.en: Verb present: -는 척하다 · Verb past: -은/ㄴ 척하다 · Adjective: -은/ㄴ 척하다 · Noun: -인 척하다

척하다=체하다 语义相同；否定用 -지 않는 척하다 / 안 -는 척하다.en: 척하다 = 체하다 (same meaning); negation uses -지 않는 척하다 / 안 -는 척하다

-는 척하다 冠形选择.en: Choosing the Adnominal Form for -는 척하다

本练习综合复习 P27 情态与语气强化章节的 8 个语法点：-기 마련이다 /.en: This exercise comprehensively reviews the 8 grammar points from the P27 Modality and Tone Reinforcement chapter: -기 마련이다 / -는 법이다 / -을/ㄹ 법하다 / -기 나름이다 / -기에 달려 있다 / -는 셈이다 / -는 셈치다 / -는 척하다.

重点辨析：-는 법이다 vs -을 법하다；-셈이다 vs -셈치다.en: Key distinctions: -는 법이다 vs -을 법하다; -셈이다 vs -셈치다

「-기(가) + 形容词/名词하다」表示\"做……是……的\"\"……起来……\.en: 「-기(가) + adjective/noun하다」 means "doing something is..." or "it is... to do." It turns a verb into a subject and is followed by an adjective that evaluates difficulty or feeling. Core expressions include: 어렵다/쉽다/힘들다/편하다/좋다, etc.

常用搭配：-기 어렵다/쉽다/힘들다/편하다/좋다/싫다；助词 -가 可省略.en: Common combinations: -기 어렵다/쉽다/힘들다/편하다/좋다/싫다; the particle -가 can be omitted

不知有多…….en: You have no idea how much...

「얼마나 + -는지/은지 + 모르다」表示\"不知有多……\"\"……得不得了.en: 「얼마나 + -는지/은지 + 모르다」 means "you have no idea how..." or "so... that it's beyond words." It is used to strongly exclaim about the depth of a degree. Although it literally means "don't know," it actually emphasizes "very" or "extremely."

얼마나 + 动词现在 -는지 / 形容词有收音 -은지 / 无收音 -ㄴ지 +.en: 얼마나 + verb present -는지 / adjective with final consonant -은지 / without final consonant -ㄴ지 + 모르다

甚至……到.en: To the point of... / Even to the extent of...

「-다 못해」表示\"……到甚至……的地步\"\"……以致于……\"。前项达到某.en: '-다 못해' means 'to the point of...' or 'so much that...'. The preceding clause reaches a certain degree, leading to a more extreme following clause. The core emphasis is on 'degree progression + exceeding the norm'.

直接接词干，不看收音；后接更极端的状态/结果.en: Attach directly to the stem regardless of final consonant; followed by a more extreme state/result

「-을/ㄹ수록」表示\"越……越……\"，随着前项程度增加，后项程度也相应变化。.en: '-을/ㄹ수록' means 'the more..., the more...'. As the degree of the preceding clause increases, the degree of the following clause changes accordingly. It is often used with '-으면 -을수록' to strengthen the emphasis.

词干：有收音 -을수록 / 无收音 -ㄹ수록 · 名词 -(이)ㄹ수록.en: Stem: with final consonant -을수록 / without final consonant -ㄹ수록 · Noun -(이)ㄹ수록

常见强调形：\"-으면 -을수록\"（越……越……）；前后主语通常一致.en: Common emphatic form: "-으면 -을수록" (the more..., the more...); the subject before and after is usually the same.

「오죽 -으면」是一种感叹反问：\"该多……啊\"\"得多么……才……\"。常与.en: 「오죽 -으면」 is an exclamatory rhetorical question: "How much...!" or "To what extent...!" It is often paired with the following clause "-겠어요/-겠니" to express a deep inference or empathy about a certain degree.

\"오죽\" 本身是\"多么/该多\"的意思；结构 \"오죽 -으면 -겠어요\.en: "오죽" itself means "how much" or "to what extent"; the structure "오죽 -으면 -겠어요" is a fixed exclamatory expression.

「-기(는) 하다」表示\"虽然……但\"\"……倒是……\"。前项承认某事实，.en: 「-기(는) 하다」 expresses "although... but" or "...indeed...". The first part acknowledges a fact, followed by a contrast or additional comment. It conveys a concessive tone and is often used with -지만/-는데.

动词/形容词词干 + -기(는) 하다 · 名词 + 이기(는) 하다.en: Verb/Adjective stem + -기(는) 하다 · Noun + 이기(는) 하다

常用形式：-기는 하다 / -기는 하지만 / -기는 한데；作让步转折.en: Common forms: -기는 하다 / -기는 하지만 / -기는 한데; used for concession or contrast

「-고말고요 / -고말고」表示\"当然……了\"\"那还用说\"\"……不用说.en: 「-고말고요 / -고말고」 means "of course...!" "that goes without saying" "needless to say...". It is used to strongly affirm or agree with what someone said, with a warm, direct, and colloquial tone. It's equivalent to "of course!" or "absolutely!" in Chinese.

直接接词干，不看收音；只用于口语回应；名词用 -이고말고요.en: Attach directly to the stem regardless of final consonant; used only in spoken responses; for nouns, use -이고말고요

「-을/ㄹ 따름이다」表示\"只是……而已\"\"不过是……\"。用于强调\"没.en: 「-을/ㄹ 따름이다」 means "just... that's all" or "merely...". It is used to emphasize the feeling of "there is nothing else, only this." The tone is formal and literary, often used in expressions of humility, regret, helplessness, or gratitude.

动词/形容词词干：有收音 -을 따름이다 / 无收音 -ㄹ 따름이다.en: Verb/Adjective stem: with final consonant -을 따름이다 / without final consonant -ㄹ 따름이다

\"따름\" 意为\"仅仅/只是\"；-을/ㄹ 따름이다 是固定搭配；名词 -(.en: "따름" means "merely/just"; -을/ㄹ 따름이다 is a fixed expression; for nouns, use -(이)ㄹ 따름이다

本练习综合复习 P28 强调与感叹深化章节的 8 个语法点：-기(가) N하다.en: This exercise comprehensively reviews the 8 grammar points from the P28 chapter on emphasis and exclamation: -기(가) N하다 / 얼마나 -는지 모르다 / -다 못해 / -을수록 / 오죽 -으면 / -기(는) 하다 / -고말고요 / -을 따름이다.

重点辨析：感叹强度阶梯 및 让步转折与限定表达.en: Key distinctions: the intensity scale of exclamations and expressions of concession/concession-contrast and limitation

「-(으)ㄴ/는 것으로 알려지다/전해지다」是新闻报道最常用的引述句式，表示\.en: 「-(으)ㄴ/는 것으로 알려지다/전해지다」 is the most common quotative pattern used in news reports, meaning "it is known," "according to reports," or "it is said." It conveys a piece of information as a "known fact" without specifying the source. 알려지다 emphasizes "widely known," while 전해지다 emphasizes "news coming in."

알려지다=被知晓；전해지다=被传告；名词 -인 것으로；否定 -지 않은 것으로.en: 알려지다 = to be known; 전해지다 = to be reported; Noun -인 것으로; Negative -지 않은 것으로

「-(으)ㄴ/는 것으로 나타나다/드러나다」表示\"（据调查/数据）显示\"\.en: 「-(으)ㄴ/는 것으로 나타나다/드러나다」 means "(according to surveys/data) it shows" or "the results indicate." 나타나다 emphasizes "showing/appearing" (neutral data), while 드러나다 emphasizes "being exposed/revealed" (hidden facts uncovered). This is a high-frequency structure in newspapers, government reports, and white papers.

나타나다=（结果）显示｜드러나다=（隐藏的）被揭露｜句尾用过去 -았/었다.en: 나타나다 = (results) show｜드러나다 = (hidden) is revealed｜Use past -았/었다 at sentence end

「-(으)ㄹ 전망이다」和「-(으)ㄹ 것으로 보이다/예상되다」都是新闻体\".en: 「-(으)ㄹ 전망이다」 and 「-(으)ㄹ 것으로 보이다/예상되다」 are both fixed expressions in news style meaning "expected/predicted." The former has a more definitive tone ("there is a prospect of..."), while the latter is more tentative ("it appears..."). They are used to express objective predictions about future trends, economic developments, and policy directions.

动词/形容词词干 + -(으)ㄹ + 전망이다｜-(으)ㄹ + 것으로 + 보이.en: Verb/Adjective stem + -(으)ㄹ + 전망이다｜-(으)ㄹ + 것으로 + 보이다 / 예상되다

有收音 -을，无收音 -ㄹ；名词 -일 전망이다；否定 -지 않을 전망이다.en: Use -을 after a final consonant, -ㄹ after no final consonant; for nouns, use -일 전망이다; for negation, use -지 않을 전망이다

「-기에 앞서 / -에 앞서」是\"在……之前\"的书面表达，比口语的 -기.en: 「-기에 앞서 / -에 앞서」 is a written expression meaning "before (doing something)," more formal than the colloquial -기 전에. It is often used in news, speeches, and report openings to indicate something that must be done before a formal action or ceremony. Verbs take -기에 앞서, and nouns take -에 앞서.

书面正式；后文常接告知/说明/致谢；不用于日常口语.en: Formal in writing; often followed by notifications, explanations, or thanks; not used in everyday speech.

「-기(를) 요구하다/촉구하다/당부하다」是新闻/公文报道公众诉求或官员发言的.en: 「-기(를) 요구하다/촉구하다/당부하다」 is a formal pattern used in news and official documents to report public demands or officials' statements. 요구하다 = to demand (strong); 촉구하다 = to urge, press (formal/media); 당부하다 = to earnestly request, appeal (polite/superior to subordinate).

助词 -를 常可省；主语多为 团体/官方；否定用 -지 않기(를).en: The particle -를 is often omitted; the subject is usually a group or official body; negation uses -지 않기(를).

仅限于/停留在.en: To be limited to / to stop at

「-는 데 그치다 / -에 그치다」表示\"仅仅停留在……\"\"只做到……为.en: 「-는 데 그치다 / -에 그치다」 means "to stop at just..." or "to only go as far as...", implying criticism or regret that something did not go further or meet expectations. It is the most common evaluative expression in news analysis and commentary. Verbs take -는 데 그치다, and nouns take -에 그치다.

句尾常用 -았/었다 表示结果；含消极评价（\"未达预期\"）.en: Often used with -았/었다 at the end to indicate a result; carries a negative evaluation ("did not meet expectations")

「-자」是\"一……就……\"的书面语连接词尾，语义与 -자마자 相近但更简洁、.en: 「-자」 is a written-language connective ending meaning "as soon as...", similar in meaning to -자마자 but more concise and formal, used specifically in written, news, or literary contexts. The actions occur in immediate succession and are often used to objectively state past events. It cannot be used with imperative or request endings.

仅接动词；主语可不同也可相同；不能与命令/请求/劝诱形式搭配；不含\"预期外\".en: Only attaches to verbs; subjects can be different or the same; cannot be used with imperative, request, or suggestion forms; does not carry an "unexpected" nuance

「이래(로) / -(으)ㄴ 이래」表示\"自从……以来（一直……）\"，比 -.en: 「이래(로) / -(으)ㄴ 이래」 means "since... (continuously up to now)" and is more formal and written in tone than -(으)ㄴ 후로 / -고 나서. Attach 이래(로) to nouns and -(으)ㄴ 이래 to the past adnominal form of verbs. It is commonly found in news retrospectives and historical statements.

이래(로) 中的 -로 可省；后文常接\"最……\"\"持续……\"\"从未…….en: The -로 in 이래(로) can be omitted; the following clause often describes a long-term state such as "the most...", "continuously...", or "never..."

本课综合 P29 全部 8 个书面/新闻体语法点：것으로 알려지다/전해지다、것.en: This lesson covers all 8 written/news-style grammar points from P29: 것으로 알려지다/전해지다, 것으로 나타나다/드러나다, -(으)ㄹ 전망이다, -기에 앞서, -기를 촉구/당부하다, -에 그치다, -자, 이래(로). Test your sensitivity to written language.

韩语里\"눈（眼睛）\"的惯用语最多、最活。掌握 눈이 높다（眼光高）、눈에 밟.en: In Korean, idioms using "눈 (eye)" are the most numerous and most commonly used. Mastering expressions like 눈이 높다 (to have high standards), 눈에 밟히다 (to linger in one's mind), 눈 밖에 나다 (to fall out of favor), and 눈이 빠지다 (to wait eagerly) marks the transition from "exam Korean" to "everyday Korean."

눈 + 助词 + 动词/形容词｜熟词组，语义与字面常不一致.en: 눈 + particle + verb/adjective | Idiomatic phrase; meaning often differs from literal words

눈이 높다 眼光高 / 눈에 밟히다 挂心上 / 눈 밖에 나다 失宠 / 눈이.en: 눈이 높다 to have high standards / 눈에 밟히다 to be on one's mind / 눈 밖에 나다 to fall out of favor / 눈이 빠지다 to wait eagerly / 눈감아 주다 to turn a blind eye

\"손（手）\"的惯用语大多与\"做事、参与、慷慨、放弃\"相关：손이 크다（大.en: Idioms with "손 (hand)" mostly relate to "doing, participating, generosity, or giving up": 손이 크다 (generous), 손을 씻다 (wash one's hands of it), 손을 놓다 (let go / stop managing), 손이 모자라다 (short-handed), 손을 대다 (get involved / start working on).

손 + 助词 + 动词｜多表\"做事/参与/放弃\".en: 손 + particle + verb | Often expresses "doing / participating / giving up"

손이 크다 大方 / 손을 씻다 洗手不干 / 손을 놓다 放手不管 / 손이.en: 손이 크다 generous / 손을 씻다 to wash one's hands of it / 손을 놓다 to let go / 손이 모자라다 to be short-handed / 손을 대다 to start working on

\"발（脚）\"的惯用语多围绕\"人脉、参与、脱身\"：발이 넓다（人脉广）、발.en: Idioms with "발 (foot)" often revolve around "connections, participation, or getting away": 발이 넓다 (well-connected), 발 벗고 나서다 (step forward / throw oneself in), 발을 빼다 (pull out / extricate oneself), 발이 묶이다 (to be tied up / stuck), 발 뻗고 자다 (sleep peacefully).

발 + 助词 + 动词｜多表\"人脉/参与/脱身/被困\".en: 발 + particle + verb ｜ Often expresses "connections / participation / getting away / being stuck"

발이 넓다 人脉广 / 발 벗고 나서다 挺身而出 / 발을 빼다 抽身 / 발.en: 발이 넓다 to have many connections / 발 벗고 나서다 to step forward actively / 발을 빼다 to pull out (of a situation) / 발이 묶이다 to be tied up / 발 뻗고 자다 to sleep soundly

\"마음（心/心情）\"和\"가슴（胸/心窝）\"是韩语情感表达的两大核心：마음.en: "마음 (heart/mind)" and "가슴 (chest/heart)" are the two core words for expressing emotions in Korean: 마음에 들다 (to like / to be to one's liking), 마음을 먹다 (to make up one's mind), 가슴이 아프다 (heartache), 가슴이 뭉클하다 (to be moved), 가슴에 새기다 (to engrave in one's heart).

마음/가슴 + 助词 + 动词/形容词｜表情感/决心.en: 마음/가슴 + particle + verb/adjective ｜ Expresses emotions / determination

마음에 들다 合心意 / 마음을 먹다 下决心 / 가슴이 아프다 心痛 / 가.en: 마음에 들다 to be to one's liking / 마음을 먹다 to make up one's mind / 가슴이 아프다 to have a heartache / 가슴이 뭉클하다 to be deeply moved / 가슴에 새기다 to engrave in one's heart

\"입（嘴）\"和\"말（话）\"的惯用语多与\"保密/传播/说话方式\"相关：.en: Idioms using "입 (mouth)" and "말 (speech)" often relate to "keeping secrets / spreading rumors / speaking style": 입이 무겁다 (to be tight-lipped), 입이 가볍다 (to be loose-lipped), 말꼬리를 잡다 (to nitpick someone's words), 말을 아끼다 (to be sparing with words), 입에 발린 말 (sweet talk / flattery).

입/말 + 助词 + 动词/形容词｜表说话方式与信任.en: 입/말 + particle + verb/adjective | Expresses manner of speech and trust

입이 무겁다 守口 / 입이 가볍다 嘴松 / 말꼬리를 잡다 抠字眼 / 말을.en: 입이 무겁다 keep a secret / 입이 가볍다 loose-lipped / 말꼬리를 잡다 nitpick / 말을 아끼다 be sparing with words / 입에 발린 말 sweet talk

\"머리（头）\"的惯用语多与思考、方案、合作、烦恼相关：머리를 굴리다（动脑筋.en: Idioms using "머리 (head)" often relate to thinking, planning, cooperation, and worries: 머리를 굴리다 (rack your brain), 머리를 맞대다 (put heads together), 머리가 아프다 (have a headache / be troubled), 머리가 잘 돌아가다 (be quick-witted), 머리를 식히다 (clear your head).

머리를 굴리다 动脑 / 머리를 맞대다 碰头 / 머리가 아프다 头疼/烦 /.en: 머리를 굴리다 rack your brain / 머리를 맞대다 put heads together / 머리가 아프다 have a headache / be troubled / 머리가 잘 돌아가다 be quick-witted / 머리를 식히다 clear your head

韩语四字成语（사자성어）多源自汉字典故，是韩语高级表达的标志。本课学与\"情感/.en: Korean four-character idioms (사자성어) mostly originate from Chinese classical stories and are a hallmark of advanced Korean expression. This lesson covers six idioms related to "emotions/attitudes/cooperation": 일석이조 (one stone, two birds), 동병상련 (misery loves company), 십시일반 (many hands make light work), 어부지리 (the fisherman's gain), 자업자득 (reap what you sow), and 우유부단 (indecisive).

四字成语作名词使用｜句中位置灵活｜多与 이다/하다 搭配.en: Four-character idioms are used as nouns | flexible position in sentences | often paired with 이다/하다

읽는 법：일석이조[일써기조] / 어부지리[어부지리]，注意汉字词双拼读法.en: Pronunciation: 일석이조[일써기조] / 어부지리[어부지리], note the double-consonant reading of Sino-Korean words

本课学与\"事态/因果/得失\"相关的六大成语：전화위복（转祸为福）、오리무중（.en: This lesson covers six idioms related to "situations/causality/gain and loss": 전화위복 (turning misfortune into fortune), 오리무중 (lost in a fog), 유비무환 (preparedness prevents calamity), 설상가상 (adding frost to snow), 고진감래 (sweet comes after bitter), and 다다익선 (the more, the better).

同前课，作名词使用 · 与 이다/하다/-으로 搭配.en: Same as the previous lesson, used as nouns | paired with 이다/하다/-으로

注意汉字对照：전화(转祸)+위복(为福) / 설상(雪上)+가상(加霜).en: Note the Chinese character correspondences: 전화(转祸)+위복(为福) / 설상(雪上)+가상(加霜)

本课综合 P30 全部 8 类惯用语/成语：눈/손/발/마음/입/머리 六大身体.en: This lesson covers all 8 types of idioms/idiomatic expressions from P30: six body parts (눈/손/발/마음/입/머리) plus 12 four-character idioms (사자성어). It tests both meaning and particle usage comprehensively.
